steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for a paper on zero-shot, text-guided explorable image super-resolution with text-to-image diffusion models. Explain why super-resolution is ill-posed, what current methods can't do, the two approaches we take, and what text guidance buys us.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- Super-resolution as an ill-posed problem; limits of current methods
- Why text is a good way to guide exploration
- Our proposal: zero-shot open-domain text-guided super-resolution, two paradigms
- Benefits shown (Fig. 1) and evaluation

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- Super-resolution as an ill-posed problem
  - recover high-quality image from LR observation \mathbf{y}; \mathbf{A} down-sampling operator, \mathbf{x} ground truth, \mathbf{n} noise
  - highly ill-posed, esp. large factors; many valid data-consistent solutions
  - supervised SOTA deep networks recover a single image (cite)
  - conditional/unconditional generative models allow sampling multiple solutions (cite)
  - exploration via graphical user inputs (cite) or semantic maps (cite)
  - but: tailored to specific classes (faces) or specific SR factors
- Why text
  - natural language simpler, more intuitive for semantic concepts
  - age, gender, emotion, race easier in text than graphical inputs
  - text guidance -> exploring semantically meaningful solutions
- Our proposal
  - first zero-shot open-domain SR with text prompts
  - diverse, semantically accurate, data-consistent reconstructions; different large downsampling factors; no training for specific degradations
  - builds on T2I generative models (cite), CLIP (cite), zero-shot diffusion-based image recovery (cite)
  - paradigm 1: adapt zero-shot diffusion SR to T2I models; open-sourced DALL-e2 (cite), Imagen (cite); different zero-shot recovery approaches (cite); handle cascade / multi-stage generation
  - paradigm 2: existing diffusion zero-shot restoration + language guidance through CLIP
  - focus: extreme SR, large upscale factors; severely ill-posed, larger solution space
- Benefits and evaluation
  - Fig. 1: existing zero-shot methods (cite) fail on complex ground truth, e.g. results of one of them (cite)
  - text recovers complex scene content matching prompt
  - face SR: more diversity in age, expression, gender, race vs. methods with limited diversity (cite)
  - evaluation: realism, fidelity to LR input, text agreement; qualitative, quantitative, human
  - benefits: flexibility, diversity, explorability; direction for text-guided exploration of image recovery

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
The goal of image super-resolution is to recover a high-quality image from a low-resolution (LR) observation \mathbf{y},

where \mathbf{A}, \mathbf{x}, and \mathbf{n} are the down-sampling operator, the ground truth image, and the measurement noise. Image super-resolution is very ill-posed, especially at large super-resolution factors, where there are many valid solutions that satisfy the data consistency accurately. Most of the recent state-of-the-art supervised deep networks for super-resolution recover only one image from this solution space, but there are also methods that use conditional or unconditional generative models, and these let you sample multiple solutions. A few of these works also let you explore the solution space, with graphical user inputs or with semantic maps. But even these methods are made for images of specific classes like faces, or they are trained for specific super-resolution factors. Natural language, on the other hand, is a simpler and more intuitive way to convey semantic concepts. For example, it is easier to give detailed descriptions or to convey concepts like age, gender, emotion, and race with text than with graphical inputs alone. So a method that guides image super-resolution with text can help a lot with exploring semantically meaningful solutions.

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
The goal of image super-resolution is to recover a high-quality image from a low-resolution (LR) observation \mathbf{y},

where \mathbf{A}, \mathbf{x}, and \mathbf{n} are the down-sampling operator, the ground truth image, and the measurement noise. Image super-resolution is very ill-posed, especially at large super-resolution factors, where there are many valid solutions that satisfy the data consistency accurately. Most of the recent state-of-the-art supervised deep networks for super-resolution recover only one image from this solution space, but there are also methods that use conditional or unconditional generative models, and these let you sample multiple solutions. A few of these works also let you explore the solution space, with graphical user inputs or with semantic maps. But even these methods are made for images of specific classes like faces, or they are trained for specific super-resolution factors. Natural language, on the other hand, is a simpler and more intuitive way to convey semantic concepts. For example, it is easier to give detailed descriptions or to convey concepts like age, gender, emotion, and race with text than with graphical inputs alone. So a method that guides image super-resolution with text can help a lot with exploring semantically meaningful solutions.

In this paper we propose, for the first time, zero-shot open-domain image super-resolution with simple and intuitive text prompts. We want to use text prompts to explore diverse and semantically accurate reconstructions that keep data consistency with the low-resolution inputs, for different large downsampling factors, and without training explicitly for these specific degradations. For this we use recent advances in text-to-image (T2I) generative models, contrastive language image pretraining (CLIP), and unsupervised zero-shot approaches to image recovery with diffusion-based generative models. We explore two paradigms for zero-shot text-guided super-resolution. In the first one, we adapt recent diffusion-based zero-shot super-resolution approaches to T2I models by changing the generative process appropriately. We take recent state-of-the-art text-to-image diffusion models, open-sourced versions of DALL-e2 and Imagen, and adapt them for zero-shot super-resolution with different zero-shot approaches for diffusion-based image recovery. These T2I models are a cascade of diffusion models at different resolutions, so we modify the zero-shot approaches to deal with the multi-stage generation. In the second approach, we modify an existing diffusion-based zero-shot restoration approach so that it has additional language guidance through CLIP. We focus on extreme image super-resolution with large upscale factors, because this problem is severely ill-posed and there is a larger solution space to explore.

Fig. 1 shows the benefits of text guidance in extreme super-resolution. Existing zero-shot methods cannot recover realistic details when the ground truth has complex content, as can be seen in the super-resolution results of one of them on a challenging input. Using text, on the other hand, makes it possible to recover complex scene content with specific details that match the text prompt. Text also easily improves the diversity of solutions for face super-resolution in age, expression, gender, race, and other attributes, compared to methods that recover images with limited diversity. We evaluate the proposed baselines for realism, fidelity with the low-resolution input, and agreement with text, in several qualitative, quantitative, and human evaluations. Extensive experiments show the benefit of using zero-shot text guidance in flexibility, diversity, and explorability of solutions to extreme super-resolution. Our work opens up a promising direction for developing efficient tools for text-guided exploration of image recovery.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
The goal of image super-resolution is to recover a high-quality image, given a low-resolution (LR) observation \mathbf{y},

where \mathbf{A}, \mathbf{x}, and \mathbf{n} represent the down-sampling operator, ground truth image, and measurement noise respectively. Image super-resolution is highly ill-posed, especially at large super-resolution factors, with many valid solutions accurately satisfying data consistency. While most recent state-of-the-art supervised deep networks for super-resolution [1,2,3] recover only a single image from this solution space, there are also methods utilizing conditional or unconditional generative models [4,5,6,7,8,9] which allow sampling multiple solutions. A few of these works also allow exploring the solution space, using graphical user inputs [4] or semantic maps [5]. Yet even these methods are tailored to images of specific classes such as faces, or are trained for specific super-resolution factors. Natural language, on the other hand, provides a simpler and more intuitive means of conveying semantic concepts. For instance, it is easier to provide detailed descriptions or convey concepts such as age, gender, emotion, and race through text than through graphical inputs alone. A method that guides image super-resolution through text can therefore greatly aid the exploration of semantically meaningful solutions.

In this paper, we propose for the first time zero-shot open-domain image super-resolution using simple and intuitive text prompts. Our goal is to explore, via text prompts, diverse and semantically accurate reconstructions that preserve data consistency with the low-resolution inputs for different large downsampling factors, without explicitly training for these specific degradations. To this end, we exploit recent advances in text-to-image (T2I) generative models [10,11,12], contrastive language image pretraining (CLIP) [13], and unsupervised zero-shot approaches to image recovery using diffusion-based generative models [14,15,9]. We explore two paradigms for zero-shot text-guided super-resolution. In the first, we adapt recent diffusion-based zero-shot super-resolution approaches to T2I models by appropriately modifying the generative process. We consider recent state-of-the-art text-to-image diffusion models, open-sourced versions of DALL-e2 [11] and Imagen [10], and adapt them for zero-shot super-resolution using different zero-shot approaches for diffusion-based image recovery [15,14,9]. Since these T2I models comprise a cascade of diffusion models at different resolutions, we modify the zero-shot approaches to deal with multi-stage generation. In the second approach, we modify an existing diffusion-based zero-shot restoration approach to incorporate additional language guidance through CLIP. We focus on extreme image super-resolution with large upscale factors, as this problem is severely ill-posed and allows exploring a larger solution space.

Fig. 1 illustrates the benefits of text guidance in extreme super-resolution. Existing zero-shot methods such as [14,16] cannot recover realistic details when the ground truth has complex content, as seen in the super-resolution results of [14] on a challenging input. In contrast, the use of text enables recovering complex scene content with specific details matching the text prompt. Text also effortlessly improves the diversity of solutions for face super-resolution in terms of age, expression, gender, race, and other attributes over [14,9], which recover images with limited diversity. We evaluate the proposed baselines in terms of realism, fidelity with the low-resolution input, and agreement with text, in several qualitative, quantitative, and human evaluations. Extensive experimental evaluations demonstrate the benefit of zero-shot text guidance in terms of flexibility, diversity, and explorability of solutions to extreme super-resolution. Our work opens up a promising direction for developing efficient tools for text-guided exploration of image recovery.
